title: Thin JetBrains adapter
description: Objective: let JetBrains discover/start the daemon and open/embed or browser-fallback to the standalone control room. Deliverable: a thin adapter with no duplicated product logic. NOT in scope: canonical state, lifecycle transitions, separate board implementation, or VS Code parity. Hard dependencies: standalone Control-room journey gate and Distribution manifest packaging. Owned paths: adapters/jetbrains/**. Verification: adapter-specific tests plus pnpm test:integration.
definitionOfDone: Adapter discovers compatible daemon/control-room distributions and fails closed on mismatch.
All product actions and rendering come from the standalone app/generated contracts.
Start, open, embed, browser fallback, reconnect, and uninstall cases pass.
taskRails: Portability consumes frozen daemon/core contracts; adapters cannot fork lifecycle or authority semantics.
Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP only; no custom MCP-over-WebSocket dialect.
Unsupported OS/provider/import facts remain typed UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN, never guessed.
IDE adapters are thin optional shells for the standalone control room. Keep files below 400 lines and use explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED. Create adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-adapter.test.ts driving the adapter with INJECTED fake ports — no real daemon spawn, no browser launch, no network. DoD 3 names six cases; each asserts the EXACT reason code AND the refusing layer from the contract's frozen tuples:
  - START: daemon absent -> start -> DAEMON_STARTED.
  - EMBED: assets present, embedding available -> CONTROL_ROOM_EMBEDDED.
  - BROWSER FALLBACK: embedding unavailable -> CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK, a SUCCESS outcome, not a failure. Most likely case to be modelled wrongly.
  - RECONNECT: a daemon already running is discovered without starting a second one -> DAEMON_RUNNING, AND assert startDaemon was NOT called. Reconnect is proven by the port not firing; asserting the code alone passes even if a second daemon was started.
  - UNINSTALL: after teardown no live handle remains and a subsequent action refuses rather than silently reopening.
  - MISMATCH (DoD 1): an incompatible distribution manifest fails CLOSED using the @moe/contracts refusal vocabulary, never an optimistic proceed.
Also: a port that THROWS becomes a typed failure at that port's layer, never an escaping exception; and DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED (started, listening unconfirmed) is a refusal, not success. Assert the sweep over IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES produced a NON-ZERO case count.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED landed. All ports are INJECTED FAKES returning canned evidence — nothing spawns a process, launches a browser or opens a socket.

RED PROVED, and I am labelling its strength honestly: `npx vitest run --root . adapters/jetbrains/src` fails at COLLECTION — "Error: Cannot find module './index.js' imported from .../jetbrains-adapter.test.ts", 1 failed suite / no tests. That is the only red available before the module exists; it proves the suite is collected and reaches for the right subject, NOT that any individual assertion is live. Per-assertion redness is step 6's job and I will not treat this as a substitute.

A DESIGN DECISION THE PLAN DID NOT ANTICIPATE, measured rather than assumed. `verifyDistributionSet` in packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-verifier.ts is the real production authority for distribution admission — it already answers API_RANGE_MISMATCH, COMPONENT_KIND_MISMATCH, COMPONENT_SET_INCOMPLETE/UNEXPECTED, COMPONENT_DUPLICATE, SIGNATURE_INVALID, SOURCE_SHA_MISMATCH, SCHEMA_HASH_MISMATCH and the digest family. IT IS NOT REACHABLE FROM HERE. Measured both ways: `grep verifyDistributionSet packages/contracts/src/index.ts` -> NOT PUBLISHED AT ROOT, and a runtime probe from adapters/jetbrains reports {"reachable":[],"unreachable":["verifyDistributionSet","decodeDistributionContainerBytes","canonicalUnsignedManifestBytes","isCanonicalText"]}. tools/packaging reaches it only by a ROOT-RELATIVE path that bypasses the exports map, which a workspace package cannot use.

So the adapter must neither delegate to it nor clone it. I scoped the adapter gate to the questions the verifier structurally CANNOT answer, so there is no forked authority:
- MANIFEST_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED — the verifier never checks manifestVersion; the parser does, and the parser is unreachable.
- COMPONENT_SET_INCOMPLETE / COMPONENT_DUPLICATE keyed by COMPONENT KIND — the verifier keys on componentId against a host-supplied expectation map. "Which kinds does a JetBrains session need" is the adapter's own requirement and belongs to no other layer.
- API_RANGE_MISMATCH against the range THIS ADAPTER was built against. The verifier compares against the HOST's expectation. An IDE plugin ships and updates independently of the distribution, so this is a second, genuinely different comparison by a different party — not a duplicate of the first.
Signature, digest and provenance verification are deliberately ABSENT from the adapter: they are the packager/startup authority, and cloning them here is exactly the fork the boundary exists to prevent. Every refusal is built by calling the real `distributionRefusal(...)` factory, so the "DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH" code and the frozen tuples are composed, never restated. refusedBy is always DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP — DISTRIBUTION_PACKAGER would be a lie about who refused.

DoD 3's SIX CASES, each pinning code AND layer:
- START — DAEMON_ABSENT licenses a start; asserts CONTROL_ROOM_EMBEDDED end to end, startDaemon called exactly once, and a separate case pins DAEMON_STARTED with its endpoint.
- EMBED — CONTROL_ROOM_EMBEDDED, outcome OK.
- BROWSER FALLBACK — CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK with outcome "OK" AND `expect("layer" in result).toBe(false)`, because a success carries no layer; modelling fallback as a failure is the plausible regression this pins.
- RECONNECT — proven by ABSENCE: startDaemon count 0, probeDaemon count 1, plus DAEMON_RUNNING. The code alone would pass even if a second daemon had been started.
- UNINSTALL — endpoint() goes from the live endpoint to null, the next openControlRoom returns DAEMON_STATE_UNKNOWN / IDE_ADAPTER / UNKNOWN, and the ENTIRE call-count record is asserted equal to its pre-uninstall value, so a silent reopen through any of the four ports reddens.
- MISMATCH — API_RANGE_MISMATCH refused before probeDaemon, startDaemon and openControlRoom (all three counts 0), because an incompatible pair must never reach the daemon.

SEVEN GATE LEGS, one fixture per predicate, and every fixture is deliberately VALID at all earlier legs — otherwise an earlier guard answers first and the leg reads as covered while never being reached. Guarded by a generation assertion (7 legs, 5 distinct reasons) so a silently emptied table cannot pass.

THROWING PORTS — three cases, one per IDE port, each asserting a DIFFERENT layer (DAEMON_DISCOVERY_PORT / DAEMON_START_PORT / CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_PORT) with a generation assertion that the three layers are distinct, so layer is a real answer rather than a constant. A throwing distribution port refuses COMPONENT_SET_INCOMPLETE: zero components were obtained, so the required set is literally incomplete — chosen because the frozen vocabulary has no discovery-port-failed reason and inventing one is barred.

Also pinned: DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED is UNKNOWN not success, AND a separate case proves the session STOPS there (openControlRoom count 0) rather than opening anyway; a refusing discovery port passes through at its own layer; absent assets

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN: adapters/jetbrains/src/index.ts plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge (`export * from "./index.ts";`, matching adapters/ide-contract/src/index.js in form). The thin session sequences the contract's three decisions and adds only what the contract deliberately left out: distribution compatibility, reconnect, and uninstall.

Order: check distribution compatibility FIRST and refuse closed on mismatch — an incompatible pair must never reach discovery; then probeDaemon -> decideDaemonDiscovery; if DAEMON_ABSENT, startDaemon -> decideDaemonStart; then openControlRoom -> decideControlRoomOpen. Return the contract's IdeAdapterResult unchanged; never re-wrap or re-code its verdicts, and never add a reason code or layer to the frozen tuples.

RECONNECT is defined by absence of action: when discovery reports a running daemon, the start port must NOT be invoked. UNINSTALL drops the session's handles so a later action refuses instead of silently reopening.

THIN MEANS THIN (DoD 2, taskRail 1): no canonical state, no lifecycle transitions, no board implementation, no product rendering. All product actions and rendering come from the standalone control room and the generated client — do not reimplement packages/control-room-client and do not fork lifecycle or authority semantics. Wrap every port call so a throw becomes a typed failure at that port's layer. Keep below 400 lines; split the compatibility gate into its own module rather than growing past it.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `npx vitest run --root . adapters/jetbrains/src` -> 1 file / 26 tests passed. `tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit` from adapters/jetbrains -> exit 0.

KEPT IN ONE MODULE, DELIBERATELY. index.ts is 218 physical lines (`grep -c ''`), inside the epic's <=250 target, so I did NOT take step 4's offer to split the compatibility gate into its own module — that offer was conditional on "rather than growing past" the cap. Splitting would also have added a second production file plus its bridge to a plan the daemon already flagged at 6 distinct files. The gate is a separately exported pure function (`admitDistribution`) inside the file, so it is independently testable and can be lifted out later without touching a call site.

SEQUENCE, exactly as specified: distribution gate -> probeDaemon/decideDaemonDiscovery -> (only when DAEMON_ABSENT) startDaemon/decideDaemonStart -> openControlRoom/decideControlRoomOpen. The gate returns before any IDE port is touched, so an incompatible pair cannot reach the daemon.

VERDICTS PASS THROUGH UNCHANGED. The three contract decision functions' results are returned as-is; nothing is re-wrapped, re-coded or re-detailed. The two vocabularies stay separate by TYPE — `JetBrainsResult = DistributionRefusal | IdeAdapterResult` — and a distribution refusal is never translated into an IDE code, nor the reverse. Every refusal I construct is typed `IdeAdapterFailure` with an `IdeAdapterReasonCode` and an `IdeAdapterLayer`, so inventing a code or layer is a compile error, not a review question. Distribution refusals come from calling the real `distributionRefusal(...)` factory, so "DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH" is never restated as a literal.

RECONNECT IS ABSENCE OF ACTION: on DAEMON_RUNNING the branch assigns the endpoint and does not reach the start port at all. UNINSTALL sets the flag and nulls the endpoint and both cached outcomes, and `openControlRoom` returns before touching a port when uninstalled.

THINNESS: no canonical state, no lifecycle transitions, no board, nothing rendered, no import of packages/control-room-client, no MCP transport of any kind. The only session state is an endpoint string, two cached verdicts and an uninstalled flag — handles, not authority.

A TYPECHECK FAILURE I FIXED PROPERLY RATHER THAN CASTING AWAY. The first tsc run failed with TS2345 at the final sweep: `result.code` widened to include "DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH", which is not a member of IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES. A cast would have silenced it; instead the sweep now THROWS if a scenario answers in the distribution vocabulary. That turned a compile error into a live assertion that the two boundaries never cross-contaminate — the test is stronger than the one I wrote in step 3.

BRIDGE: adapters/jetbrains/src/index.js is `export * from "./index.ts";` with a trailing LF and no CR, verified byte by byte with `od -c` (last bytes `"   ;  \n`, 28 bytes total), matching adapters/ide-contract/src/index.js in form. Noting for the record that the bridge is NOT the mechanism for root reachability — the exports map is; the bridge is repo convention and is enforced by the audit tests coming in step 5.

Runtime entrypoint probe landed, mechanism copied from adapters/ide-contract/src/ide-adapter-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts. Suite is now 2 files / 33 tests passed; typecheck exit 0.

Mechanism identical: execFileAsync(process.execPath, ["--experimental-strip-types", "--input-type=module", "-e", source], { cwd: PACKAGE_ROOT, timeout: 20_000 }), 30s per-test budget, child killed on timeout rather than left to outlive the run. cwd at the package root is what makes `@moe/jetbrains-adapter` resolve through this package's own exports map by Node's self-reference rule, and the two dependency specifiers resolve through THIS package's node_modules — which is precisely what turns them into edge proofs instead of symbol-presence checks.

THE THREE REQUIRED ASSERTIONS, each on VALUES because strip-types erases every `export type`:
1. ROOT ENTRY: {"outcome":"IMPORTED","hasNamedExports":true,"undefinedBindingCount":0,"createSessionType":"function","admitType":"function","requiredKinds":["CONTROL_ROOM","DAEMON"]}. undefinedBindingCount is the load-bearing one — an import cycle yields a TDZ-undefined binding that imports cleanly and only fails at first use, so a non-empty namespace is not proof.
2. @moe/ide-adapter-contract FROM this package: reasonCodeCount 14, layerCount 4, decideDaemonStart typeof "function". Counts are pinned rather than merely non-zero, so a shrunken vocabulary reddens.
3. @moe/contracts FROM this package: DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION "moe-distribution-manifest/1", distributionRefusal typeof "function", and the function is CALLED — the probe asserts the whole returned object {"code":"DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH","ok":false,"reason":"API_RANGE_MISMATCH","refusedBy":"DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP"}. Calling it is the difference between "the name is present" and "the value survived to runtime". This is the exact specifier and the exact two symbols that produced TS2305 before the barrel published them.

NEGATIVE CONTROL present and passing: importing "./src/jetbrains-adapter.test.js" fails with the LITERAL "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND", not merely "it threw". It does double duty — proves test-tier code was kept off the runtime surface, and proves the three positive probes can still detect a failure rather than passing vacuously.

Also carried over the four BRIDGE AUDIT tests from the contract package, since a missing or CRLF bridge is invisible to every in-process suite: bridges exactly the non-test modules (with expected>0 and excluded>0 vacuity floors, and the bridge content compared as bytes so a CRLF bridge lands in wrongContent); excludes every test module for a NAMED reason, pinned to exactly {"jetbrains-adapter.test.ts":"test-file","jetbrains-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts":"test-file"}; and bridges every module reachable from the entry point by walking relative `.js` specifiers.

implementationPlan.description:
Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. Each must redden a NAMED test; record the failing assertion. (a) Skip the distribution compatibility gate so an incompatible pair proceeds — the DoD 1 mismatch case must redden. (b) Call startDaemon even when discovery reports DAEMON_RUNNING — the reconnect case must redden, proving it asserts the port was NOT called. (c) RE-CODE BROWSER FALLBACK AS A FAILURE — mapped CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK to failure(CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_REFUSED). 2 red: "BROWSER FALLBACK: unavailable embedding is a SUCCESS, not a failure" (expected a 4-key object to equal a 3-key one — the extra key is `layer`, which a success must not carry) and the vocabulary sweep.
